# Stop Slop — strip the AI tells out of your prose

Curated by Skill Harbor: a plain-instructions skill — no scripts, no tools, no MCP, no account — that teaches an agent to remove predictable AI writing patterns from prose. Its 8 core rules: cut filler phrases; break formulaic structures; active voice with a human subject; be specific, with no vague declaratives and no lazy extremes like 'every / always / never'; put the reader in the room; vary rhythm, mixing sentence lengths; trust readers, with no softening or hand-holding; and cut quotables — if it sounds like a pull-quote, rewrite it. A Quick Checks list turns the rules into a pre-delivery pass: adverbs, passive voice, inanimate subjects doing human verbs, Wh- sentence starters, throat-clearing, 'not X, it's Y' contrasts, matched sentence lengths, punchy one-liner paragraph endings, em dashes, vague declaratives, narrator-from-a-distance voice, and meta-joiners. Scoring rates 1–10 on Directness, Rhythm, Trust, Authenticity, and Density; below 35/50, revise. The skill bans em dashes outright and bans all adverbs — a user who likes either will fight the skill. That is a feature of the skill, not a bug softened in this fiche.
